title: Phone: Kestrel Springs Pump Station Fuel at 18%, Fuel Tender Held at CR 68

fields.orgName: Sawmill County Office of Emergency Management

caller.name: Ray Lindqvist
caller.label: Operations Superintendent, Pine Gulch Water District

transcript.speaker: Ray Lindqvist (Water District)
transcript.text: EOC, this is Ray Lindqvist at the water district. I need the Fire Chief and the Sheriff on this if you can get them. It's the Kestrel Springs pump station.

transcript.speaker: Ray Lindqvist (Water District)
transcript.text: The generator fuel gauge just read 18 percent. With the hydrant draw we've got right now, that's two hours fifty minutes. So the station runs dry around 21:20.

transcript.speaker: Ray Lindqvist (Water District)
transcript.text: And the tank is dropping four feet an hour. Engine 31 and the strike team, ST-CO-4417, are pulling hydrants hard on Kestrel Springs Road. Once that pump quits, those hydrants lose pressure. The upper ones go first.

transcript.speaker: Ray Lindqvist (Water District)
transcript.text: Here's the part that matters. Your fuel truck, the High Plains Fuel tender we asked for, is sitting at the CR 68 traffic control point. It's not moving. I need somebody to get it to my station, or tell me what the plan is if it can't get there.

transcript.speaker: Ray Lindqvist (Water District)
transcript.text: And no, I can't wait on the co-op. Circuit 12 to the station is still dead, and nobody's given me a time.

transcript.speaker: RCC Dispatcher
transcript.text: EOC, Regional Communications Center. 2-Sam-21 is asking for you about that fuel truck. I'm patching him onto this line now.

transcript.speaker: Deputy Sgt. Alana Whitcomb (2-Sam-21, radio patch)
transcript.text: County, 2-Sam-21 at the CR 68 TCP. I've got a High Plains Fuel tender here with five hundred gallons of diesel. The driver says he's headed to the Kestrel Springs pump station.

transcript.speaker: Deputy Sgt. Alana Whitcomb (2-Sam-21, radio patch)
transcript.text: CR 68 east is Closed on the 17:00 list, and the smoke is down at the shoulder. I'm not letting a civilian fuel truck in there without an escort and an OK from fire.

transcript.speaker: Deputy Sgt. Alana Whitcomb (2-Sam-21, radio patch)
transcript.text: Driver says he'll wait twenty minutes, then he's going home. What do you want me to do with him?

voiceStyles.Ray Lindqvist (Water District): Man in his 50s, calm but clipped, a utility veteran working the numbers. Speaks fast and sounds tired. A small control room hums behind him.
voiceStyles.RCC Dispatcher: Woman in her 30s, flat and efficient dispatcher cadence, brief.
voiceStyles.Deputy Sgt. Alana Whitcomb (2-Sam-21, ra: Man in his 40s on a handheld radio, wind gusting behind him. Firm and measured, with short bursts between keying the mic.

instructorNote: This tests whether the Fire Chief/UC picks either an escorted fuel run under Controlled road rules or a backup water plan (tender shuttle, drafting, or a portable pump through interagency dispatch) before the 20-minute deadline, and plans for hydrants losing pressure. Look for the Sheriff tying any escort to fire clearing the route, and for EM logging the decision, putting the road change on the shared list, and keeping the Circuit 12 request to the co-op on hold, since restoration needs a patrol and gusts below 35 mph.
